does: Beats air into egg whites or cream until they hold a peak.

intro.what: Whipping incorporates air until a foam can hold a peak; this method describes egg whites.
intro.why: It teaches you to distinguish a glossy supporting foam from a dry overworked one.

how: Start with a clean, dry bowl, with no trace of fat or yolk in it.
Whisk slowly at first, until the whites are a loose foam.
Speed up, lifting the whisk through the foam in big circles.
Stop as soon as the foam stands in a peak when the whisk is lifted.

cues.text: Glossy and smooth. A peak stands on the lifted whisk, its tip bending slightly.
The bowl can be tipped without the foam sliding.

mistakes.mistake: Whipping past the peak, so that the foam turns dry and grainy and leaks water.
mistakes.fix: Stop at a glossy peak. Whites that have gone grainy cannot be brought back.

mistakes.mistake: A trace of yolk or grease in the bowl, so that the whites never rise.
mistakes.fix: Separate each egg over a small bowl first, and wipe the mixing bowl clean.

quiz.question: What does whipping egg whites build?
choices: A smooth liquid with no incorporated air.
A firm cooked sheet of egg.
An airy foam that holds a peak.
quiz.because: Whisking incorporates air into a structure that can support a peak rather than simply blend the liquid.

quiz.question: How should the egg-white bowl be prepared?
choices: Clean and dry without grease or yolk.
Lightly greased so the foam releases.
Coated with egg yolk before adding whites.
quiz.because: Grease or yolk interferes with the rise of an egg-white foam.

quiz.question: Which appearance marks the intended peak here?
choices: Dry and grainy with leaking liquid.
Glossy and smooth with a slightly bending tip.
A liquid mixture that runs flat immediately.
quiz.because: The peak should have structure while the foam retains gloss and smoothness.

quiz.question: Whites turn dry and grainy after the peak stage. What should change next time?
choices: Keep beating until the grains disappear.
Wait for liquid to leak out before stopping.
Stop at the glossy peak instead of continuing.
quiz.because: Continuing beyond the desired peak damages the smooth foam rather than strengthening it.

variant_of.differs: The aim is air. Whisking goes on until the foam holds a peak.
